item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Project Operations - Define the accounting date at invoice level
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to define the accounting date at the invoice level in Dynamics 365 Project Operations. This feature will reach public preview on September 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
With this feature, users can set the accounting date on an invoice separately from the transaction and document dates, so the billed revenue posts to the right financial period. This keeps Project Operations and Finance and operations apps in sync, with the same accounting date flowing through for consistent billed sales postings.

Key capabilities of this feature include:
  • Introduces an accounting date field on the invoice that you can define.
  • Sets a user-defined accounting date on the billed sales actuals, which is passed to Finance and operations apps, so the transaction is aligned to the same date.
  • Lets the accounting date differ from the transaction or document date to give you control over period alignment.
  • Lets the system fall back to the invoice confirmation date if the accounting date is not defined (existing default behavior).
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Define the accounting date at invoice level.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Automate - Create and manage custom dashboard tiles
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to create and manage custom dashboard tiles in Power Automate. This feature will reach public preview on September 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature enables users to monitor the metrics that matter most to their role or team without relying on external tools. By allowing personalized visualizations directly within Automation Center, users can gain faster insights, improve operational visibility, and make more informed decisions.

Users can add, edit, delete, and reorder personal custom tiles across supported Automation Center dashboards, including Runs, Work Queues, Machines, and Errors. Each tile can be configured with a name, optional description, selected query, and visualization type such as bar, line, area, pie, table, or metric card. A built-in test capability allows users to preview the data before saving the tile. Custom tiles are available through edit mode, where users can manage their layout within a dedicated section of the dashboard.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Create and manage custom dashboard tiles .

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Manage overnight shifts as a single continuous schedule
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to manage overnight shifts as a single continuous schedule in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 2, 2026.

How does this affect me?
With this feature, supervisors can now create and manage overnight shifts that span across midnight while maintaining a single continuous shift experience. Activities, breaks, meals, and ad-hoc work can be scheduled anywhere within the overnight shift and remain part of a single continuous itinerary. Supervisors can view and manage the entire shift without manually splitting schedules across calendar days. Activities that cross midnight are preserved as a single record and are not divided into separate activities.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [planForChange] Manage who can upload advanced agents and plugins
item.description:
[What and Why:]

To help organizations manage the deployment of advanced Copilot extensibility scenarios, we are introducing a new admin control that determines who can upload advanced agents and plugins. This enhancement strengthens enterprise governance and manageability by allowing administrators to limit advanced-package uploads to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups while maintaining flexibility for organizations that want broader access.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  1. General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins September 25th
  2. Expected completion by the end of October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  1. Microsoft 365 administrators responsible for managing Copilot agents and plugins.
  2. Organizations that allow users to upload advanced agents or plugins.
  3. Users who create or upload advanced agents and plugins after this feature becomes available.

Platforms/Services:

  1. Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork surfaces
  2. Copilot agents
  3. Copilot plugins
  4. Microsoft Entra ID

What will happen:

  1. On September 25th, the control will be visible in MAC (see Advanced package uploads screenshot) and admins will have until October 25th to select their preference of all users, no users or specific users or groups.
  2. Starting October 25th, Advanced-package uploads will be enabled by default unless the admin has selected no users or specific users or groups.
  3. Admins can configure uploads for all users, selected users, Entra ID groups, or no users.
  4. Basic package uploads remain allowed and are not impacted.
  5. The setting applies only to advanced agents and plugins uploaded after the control becomes available.
  6. No action is required to maintain current behavior,

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  1. Review the advanced-package upload setting when it becomes available on September 25th.
  2. Determine whether advanced-package uploads should be available to all users, selected users, groups, or no users prior to October 25th.
  3. Update internal administrator and help desk documentation as needed.
  4. Inform support teams of the new governance control.
  5. If no action is taken, advanced-package uploads remain allowed by default.

[Compliance Considerations:]

  1. The change introduces new administrative governance controls for advanced agents and plugins.
  2. The feature supports administration through Microsoft Entra ID group membership.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Insights Copilot Analytics cowork adoption impact
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing Cowork adoption and impact insights in the Consumption dashboard in Copilot Analytics to help organizations understand how Microsoft 365 Copilot Cowork capabilities are adopted and how they influence work outcomes across the organization. These insights provide leaders, managers, and analysts with actionable visibility into usage patterns, what tasks users are completing using Cowork, and an estimate of how much additional work was made possible using Cowork (Cowork assisted hours). These insights enable data-driven decisions and help organizations optimize their Copilot investments. This update also extends Cowork metrics into Advanced Insights in Viva Insights for deeper analysis and custom reporting.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Available now

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Leaders including executives
  • Managers with scoped organizational access
  • Insights Analysts with global partition access
  • Global administrators

Platforms and Services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Copilot Analytics
  • Viva Insights Advanced Insights
  • Web

What will happen

  • Cowork adoption and impact insights will be enabled by default for all eligible roles.
  • Users can find the experience on the Microsoft 365 services tab in the Consumption dashboard. In the Credit usage breakdown by service section, select Deep dive next to Cowork.
  • The feature is available to all Microsoft 365 tenants.
  • Organizations must have at least 50 Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users to view these insights.
  • Eligible viewers do not need their own Microsoft 365 Copilot license to access the insights.
  • Leaders will have access to tenant-level views showing organization-wide adoption and impact.
  • All eligible roles can view tenant-wide Cowork adoption and impact insights in the My company view.
  • Cowork credits used cost data will not be surfaced in tenant-level views.
  • Managers will see adoption and impact insights scoped to their organizations.
  • Insights Analysts will be able to access Cowork usage metrics through Advanced Insights using standard person queries.
  • Analysts can export data to CSV, connect to Power BI, or use Microsoft Fabric for custom reporting.
  • Global administrators can manage access using the Copilot dashboard VFAM control.
  • Disabling this control turns off the entire Copilot dashboard experience, not just Cowork insights.

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review whether Cowork adoption and impact insights should remain enabled, as this feature is on by default.
  • If needed, disable access using the Copilot dashboard VFAM control in Copilot dashboard settings.
  • Prepare Insights Analysts to use Advanced Insights standard person queries for cowork usage reporting.
  • Inform leaders and managers about the availability of adoption and impact insights.
  • Update internal documentation and training materials related to Copilot Analytics if applicable.

Learn more

  • How to use the Consumption Dashboard in Insights | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as usual for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Outlook: Change the organizer of meetings
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing Change organizer for eligible Outlook meetings and recurring meeting series. Users can ask another person in their organization to become the organizer, and the selected person must accept before ownership changes. This supports personal and team productivity by maintaining meeting continuity during role changes, leave, and offboarding.

[Rollout Schedule:]

Phase 1 supports eligible non-online meetings:

  • Worldwide: Late September through late October 2026
  • GCC: Early October through late October 2026
  • GCC High: Early November through late November 2026
  • DoD: Early November through late November 2026

Phase 2 will add eligible online meetings. For Teams meetings, the transfer will generate a new Teams meeting link owned by the new organizer. Phase 3 will add transfer support for eligible Teams meeting artifacts, including chat, meeting options, transcripts, recordings, agenda, notes, and attendance reports. Phase 2 and Phase 3 timing will be announced separately.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who organize eligible meetings or recurring series.
  • Users selected to become a new organizer.
  • Delegates with permission to edit meetings on another user's primary calendar.
  • Help desk teams supporting meeting ownership transitions.

Platforms/Services:

  • Outlook on the web
  • New Outlook for Windows
  • Teams Microsoft 365 Calendar
  • Exchange Online

Classic Outlook for Windows is not supported.

What will happen:

  • The current organizer can select one person in the same organization or tenant and send an organizer change request.
  • The meeting remains with the current organizer until the selected person accepts.
  • The organizer or an authorized delegate can cancel a pending request.
  • For recurring series, future instances move to the new organizer's calendar. Earlier instances remain with the previous organizer.
  • The previous organizer is not automatically added as an attendee.
  • Internal Exchange Online attendees receive a silent update and do not need to respond again. Their Reminder, Category, Show As, and Private settings are preserved.
  • External and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and a new invitation, which requires a response.
  • The meeting body, attachments, and sensitivity labels are preserved. The new organizer might require separate access to OneDrive attachments or links.
  • Phase 1 does not support online or Teams meetings.
  • This feature is enabled by default and requires no tenant configuration.

The meeting must be in the future, use a work or school account, and be stored on the organizer's primary calendar. Draft, canceled, encrypted, group calendar, group mailbox, and shared mailbox meetings are not eligible.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No administrative action is required.

  • Review meeting ownership processes for role changes, leave, and offboarding.
  • Inform help desk teams that Phase 1 supports only eligible non-online meetings.
  • Update internal meeting management and offboarding documentation.
  • Tell users that the new organizer must accept the request and that the previous organizer is not automatically retained as an attendee.
  • Advise users that external attendees must respond to a replacement invitation.
  • Ask users to confirm that the new organizer can access linked OneDrive content.
  • Prepare users for a new Teams meeting link when online meeting transfers become available.
  • Review the Microsoft Support article, Change the organizer of a meeting in Outlook.

[Compliance Considerations:]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Future meeting instances move to the new organizer's calendar and can be managed by that organizer. Earlier recurring instances remain with the previous organizer. Meeting content is preserved, but linked OneDrive content might require separate access.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?The feature adds organizer transfer requests within an organization. Internal attendees receive silent updates, while external and on-premises attendees receive a cancellation and replacement invitation.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft SharePoint: PowerShell support for brand fonts deletion
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft SharePoint is introducing PowerShell support for deleting brand font files from the Brand Fonts library used by the SharePoint Brand Center. With the new Remove-SPOFontFile cmdlet, SharePoint administrators can remove brand font files that are no longer approved, licensed, or needed across their organization in SharePoint.

This cmdlet is the supported deletion path for brand fonts for SharePoint. It is designed to help admins manage font lifecycle and avoid cross-geo inconsistencies by removing font copies across the primary geo and satellite geos.

When a deleted font is referenced by existing SharePoint sites or pages, the content will continue to be rendered using a Microsoft-defined fallback font. Font packages that reference deleted fonts are not automatically deleted. They remain available for use, but a warning message is displayed when required fonts are unavailable.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Note: Brand font management in Brand Center currently depends on the SharePoint Public CDN and is available only to customers who have Public CDN enabled.

  • SharePoint administrators can manage brand font deletion via PowerShell, helping organizations govern SharePoint brand fonts lifecycle, licensing, and compliance. The cmdlet removes font copies across the primary geo and satellite geos, helping avoid cross-geo inconsistencies.
  • End-user content remains readable. If a deleted font is referenced by an existing site or page, SharePoint will use the Microsoft-defined fallback fonts.
  • Font packages that reference deleted fonts remain available, with status shown to indicate unavailable font references.

Example results of running the cmdlet

Before deleting the font

After deleting the font

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Review the official documentation for PowerShell branding governance:
    • Remove-SPOFontFile (Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
    • Brand fonts - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • After rollout is complete, upgrade your PowerShell module to the required version before using these new features.
  • Review the current fonts in the Brand Center and identify fonts that are no longer approved, licensed, or needed.
  • Coordinate with brand managers and SharePoint site owners before deleting fonts that may affect site branding.
  • Update internal documentation and admin procedures for managing brand fonts with PowerShell.

item.title: [stayInformed] [Outlook Mobile] Purview Data Loss Prevention support for Calendar Events
item.description:
[What and why:]

Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention \(DLP\) policies for calendar events. Organizations can detect and help prevent the sharing of sensitive information in meeting subjects, descriptions, and invite content through policy tips, user remediation, and policy enforcement. This provides consistent compliance protection across email and calendar experiences on mobile devices.

[Rollout schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by late September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

This feature helps organizations extend Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention protections to calendar events created from Outlook for iOS and Android. Users receive policy guidance before sending meeting invitations that contain sensitive information, helping reduce accidental data exposure and improve compliance. Organizations benefit from more consistent protection across email and calendar workflows while supporting regulatory and corporate data protection requirements.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

No administrator action is required to prepare for this feature. Existing Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention policies will automatically apply to supported calendar events in Outlook for iOS and Android. Organizations with DLP policies already configured can benefit from expanded protection of calendar content without additional policy creation or client configuration. Administrators may choose to review existing DLP policies to ensure they align with their organization's compliance requirements.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Edge: Upgraded Copilot new tab page
item.description:
Updated September 14, 2026: We have updated the timeline and content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Edge is introducing an upgraded Copilot new tab page that brings Microsoft 365 Copilot chat, web search, and work content into a single experience. Users can search the web, navigate to websites, interact with Microsoft 365 Copilot, and access relevant work content from a single experience.

The updated experience includes enhanced Copilot chat integration, compose capabilities, suggested actions, curated work content, and a refreshed design to help users complete tasks more efficiently.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566703.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview: Beginning in late September 2026 (previously early September) and expected to complete by mid-October 2026 (previously mid-September)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-September) and expect to complete by early November 2026 (previously mid-September)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in your organization who have the Copilot new tab page enabled in Microsoft Edge.
  • Users who do not have the Copilot new tab page enabled will continue to see the existing new tab page experience.
  • To access this experience, users must have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Edge
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

The Copilot new tab page is off by default.

When enabled, users will see:

  • An updated search box for navigating to websites, searching the web, or sending a query to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
  • Enhanced Copilot chat and compose capabilities.
  • Suggested actions and work content to help users begin and complete tasks.
  • Work cards that may surface organizational content such as files and calendar events.
  • A refreshed design, app launcher, pinned quick links, and updated theme settings.
  • Starting in September 2026, Discover feed and feed toggle functionality will be limited. We plan to continue improving and expanding these capabilities as the Copilot new tab page evolves
  • A Discover feed with curated news and content where supported.

Admins can enable the Copilot new tab page through the Microsoft Edge management service using the CopilotNewTabPageEnabled policy and assign the configuration to all users or selected Microsoft Entra groups.

Depending on organizational policy settings, users may be able to disable the experience after it has been enabled.

Users who are not enabled will continue to see the existing Microsoft Edge new tab page.

[Action required and recommendations]

The Copilot new tab page is off by default. No admin action required before rollout as this change applies only to organizations that enabled the Copilot new tab page via CopilotNewTabPageEnabled. If your organization has enabled this policy, users will automatically see the upgraded Copilot new tab page. If the policy is not configured or is disabled, there is no change to your users' new tab page experience.

If your organization plans to enable the experience, we recommend that you:

  • Review your current Microsoft Edge and Copilot new tab page configuration.
  • Determine which users or Microsoft Entra groups should receive the experience.
  • Verify that affected users have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Evaluate the effect of surfacing organizational files and calendar events through work cards.
  • Review applicable AI governance and compliance requirements before enabling the experience.
  • Notify affected users about the updated new tab page.
  • Update relevant user guidance, training, and support documentation.

Learn more

  • Configure the Copilot new tab page | Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, ML, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The upgraded Copilot new tab page integrates Microsoft 365 Copilot chat and can surface organizational content, including files and calendar events, through work cards and suggested prompts.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can send queries directly to Microsoft 365 Copilot from the new tab page search box and access integrated Copilot chat functionality within the Microsoft Edge new tab experience.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can enable the Copilot new tab page through the Microsoft Edge management service and assign the configuration to all users or selected Microsoft Entra groups.
Can users enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Depending on organizational settings, users may be able to turn off the Copilot new tab page experience and switch between Work cards and Chat chips.
Can the feature be controlled through Microsoft Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can assign the Copilot new tab page configuration to one or more Microsoft Entra groups.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Entra ID: Passkey support for B2B users
item.description:
Updated September 14, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra ID will support passkey registration and sign-in for B2B users, including internal guest users and external users. Eligible B2B users will be able to register and use passkeys issued by the resource tenant to satisfy that tenant's multifactor authentication (MFA) requirements.

Passkeys are already supported for member users in their home tenant. Until now, B2B users could not use a resource tenant passkey when that tenant required MFA and did not trust the home tenant's MFA. This update closes that gap and gives guest and external users a phishing-resistant way to satisfy MFA requirements in the resource tenant.

B2B users can register a resource tenant passkey from the resource tenant's My Security Info page, during a proof-up prompt, or through a passkey registration campaign. Once registered, the passkey can satisfy the resource tenant's MFA requirements during sign-in.

Microsoft Authenticator app passkeys will be supported for internal guest users but not for external users.

Important: This rollout intersects with the previously announced retirement of SMS and voice authentication. As described in Message Center posts MC1426371 and MC1434201, any user enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies will be automatically enabled for all passkey types. This will include eligible B2B users when B2B passkey support becomes available.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (GCC, Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by late February 2027

  • Internal guest users: Beginning in early October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026
  • External users (excluding Microsoft Authenticator app passkeys): Rollout timing will be communicated in a future Message center post update.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Entra administrators managing Authentication methods policies
  • Organizations that use Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration
  • Internal guest users and external users who are in scope for passkey authentication
  • Internal guest users and external users who are enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • My Security Info
  • Authentication methods policy
  • Conditional Access

What will happen

  • The feature will be enabled by default.
  • B2B users who are already in scope for passkeys in your Authentication methods policy will automatically be able to register and sign in with resource tenant passkeys.
  • Eligible B2B users may receive prompts to register a passkey during sign-in through proof-up experiences or passkey registration campaigns, if those experiences are configured in your tenant.
  • Users can also register a passkey from the resource tenant's My Security Info page.
  • If your organization has excluded B2B users from passkeys in the Authentication methods policy, and those users are not separately subject to automatic passkey enablement through the SMS and voice retirement changes, they will not be prompted and will not be able to register or sign in with a resource tenant passkey.
  • Under the SMS and voice retirement changes described in MC1426371 and MC1434201, B2B users who are enabled for SMS or voice in the Authentication methods policy or legacy MFA policies will be automatically enabled for all passkey types. Excluding these users from the passkey policy alone will not prevent this automatic enablement if they remain enabled for SMS or voice.
  • This change gives guest and external users a phishing-resistant sign-in option and helps organizations extend strong authentication requirements to their B2B population.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that administrators review current passkey and MFA configurations before rollout:

  • Review your Authentication methods policy. Confirm which users are in scope for passkeys, including guest and external users. B2B users who are in scope will be enabled automatically. Exclude them from the policy if that is not the intended behavior.
  • Review Message Center posts MC1426371 and MC1434201 for details about the SMS and voice retirement changes.
  • Review SMS and voice assignments in both the Authentication methods policy and legacy MFA policies. If you do not want specific B2B users to be automatically enabled for all passkey types, move those users off SMS and voice in all applicable policies. Excluding them only from the passkey policy is not sufficient while they remain enabled for SMS or voice.
  • Review your passkey registration campaign. Confirm that the campaign's user scope includes the intended users.
  • Review your Conditional Access policies. Confirm that MFA and authentication strength requirements will apply as intended for B2B users when resource tenant passkeys become available.
  • Confirm user scoping across authentication-related policies. Make sure the groups and user types targeted by each policy align with your organization's requirements for guest and external users.

Consider notifying your help desk and identity support teams that eligible B2B users may begin receiving passkey registration prompts after rollout.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Passkey credential registration data may be stored as part of Microsoft Entra authentication management.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?The change introduces an additional authentication method for B2B users accessing resource tenant resources.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Entra: Users can register a passkey or passwordless sign-in as their first multifactor authentication method
item.description:

[What and why]

Users will soon be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor authentication method. Previously, people had to set up an alternate MFA method like SMS or Voice before they could add a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO. That extra step pushed users toward weaker methods and slowed the move to phishing-resistant sign-in. Now password-only users can go straight to a passkey, making it easier to adopt strong authentication from day one. As part of this work, we will also be enabling Authenticator App passwordless sign-in to be a user's first registered MFA method. 

[Rollout schedule]

This feature will roll out in phases: 

Phase 1: Support for synced passkeys, Microsoft Entra passkeys on Windows, and FIDO2 security keys.  

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026. 

Phase 2: Support for Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, Authenticator App passkey, and Authenticator App passwordless sign-in. 

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): We will begin rolling out in early January 2026 and expect to complete by late February 2027. 

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who have not yet registered a multifactor authentication method
  • Identity and security administrators responsible for authentication onboarding and registration policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Passkeys (FIDO2)
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Microsoft Authenticator passwordless sign-in

What will happen

  • Password-only users will be able to register passkeys or passwordless sign-in as their first MFA method.
  • Users will no longer need to register a method such as SMS or voice before registering a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO, or Authenticator passwordless sign-in.
  • Organizations may see reduced registration friction and increased adoption of phishing-resistant authentication methods.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required for this change.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Review Conditional Access policies related to security information registration.
  • Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.
  • Review onboarding and registration guidance so users know to set up a passkey as their preferred first method.

Learn more 

  • (To be updated closer to rollout) Register a synced passkey (FIDO2) | Authentication | Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can control which authentication methods users are allowed to register through existing Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access policies.
Does the change affect access or authentication controls?Yes. The update changes how users register multifactor authentication methods by allowing eligible users to register supported passkeys or passwordless authentication methods as their first MFA method.
Can administrators govern the feature through existing Microsoft Entra controls?Yes. Administrators retain control over the feature through Microsoft Entra authentication method policies and Conditional Access configurations.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Microsoft Graph: User.ReadBasic.All will no longer allow reading user app role assignments and license details
item.description:
[What and why]

We are correcting the behavior of the Microsoft Graph delegated and app-only permission User.ReadBasic.All. This permission is intended to provide access only to a limited set of basic user profile properties. However, it currently also allows access to user app role assignments and license details.

To address a security vulnerability, we are removing access to user app role assignments and license details from User.ReadBasic.All and aligning the permission with its intended scope. This is not a breaking change for applications that use User.ReadBasic.All only for its intended purpose of accessing basic user profile information.

Applications that rely on this unintended access should be updated with the appropriate least-privileged permissions before rollout is complete.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

Organizations are affected if their applications use the Microsoft Graph delegated or app-only permission User.ReadBasic.All to read:

  • User app role assignments
  • User license details

Developers, application owners, and administrators responsible for managing application permissions in Microsoft Entra ID should review this change.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Graph
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Applications using Microsoft Graph permissions

What will happen

  • Applications granted only User.ReadBasic.All will no longer be able to read user app role assignments or user license details.
  • Applications that access only basic user properties, such as display name, email address, and department, will continue to function without changes.
  • Affected applications may experience failures or permission-related errors after the change is applied.
  • Users may experience application disruptions if an application has only User.ReadBasic.All but attempts to access user app role assignments or license details.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action is required if you have applications that use User.ReadBasic.All to access user app role assignments or license details.

Recommended actions:

  • Review applications granted User.ReadBasic.All in the Microsoft Entra admin center under Enterprise applications > Permissions or in your internal application catalog.
  • Identify applications that use this permission to read user app role assignments or user license details.
  • Update affected applications to use the appropriate least-privileged permissions:
    • To read user app role assignments: User.Read.All
    • To read user license details: LicenseAssignment.Read.All
    • To read both: User.Read.All
  • Obtain administrator consent for the new permissions, update application configurations, redeploy affected applications, and test impacted scenarios.
  • Notify developers and application owners of the upcoming permission changes and rollout schedule.
  • Monitor application logs and Microsoft Graph API responses for permission-related errors after rollout.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Microsoft Exchange Online: Review and configure EWSAllowedAppIDs before Exchange Web Services access changes
item.description:
Updated September 11, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

As part of the final phase of Exchange Web Services (EWS) retirement, Microsoft is updating how the EWSAllowedAppIDs setting is applied in Exchange Online. This change is designed to help organizations identify and manage applications that still require EWS access while reducing the risk of unexpected service disruption.

Organizations that continue to use EWS should review and maintain their own EWSAllowedAppIDs list. If a tenant administrator has already configured this list, Microsoft will not overwrite or modify it.

Beginning on October 1, 2026, Microsoft will start enabling this updated behavior by cloud as part of the EWS retirement rollout.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by late April 2027

The updated behavior will apply when the rollout reaches your cloud.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that continue to use Exchange Web Services (EWS)
  • Exchange Online administrators responsible for managing EWS access
  • Tenants with EWSEnabled set to True or Null

Platforms and services

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Web Services (EWS)

What will happen

After the updated behavior is enabled in a cloud:

  • EWS will require a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list when EWSEnabled is set to True.
  • Before enabling the change, Microsoft will ensure that tenants with EWSEnabled already set to True have an EWSAllowedAppIDs list.
  • If a customer-managed list does not exist, Microsoft will generate a list based on EWS application usage observed during the previous 60 days to help reduce the risk of service interruption.
  • Microsoft-generated lists may omit applications that run infrequently and may include applications that no longer require EWS access.
  • If EWSEnabled remains Null, Microsoft will populate EWSAllowedAppIDs only when a customer-managed list does not already exist. This will occur shortly before Microsoft updates EWSEnabled to False as part of the retirement rollout.
  • Microsoft will not modify an EWSAllowedAppIDs list that has already been configured by a tenant administrator.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization still relies on EWS, we recommend taking the following actions as soon as possible:

  • Review EWS usage from the previous 60 days and identify all applications that require continued EWS access, including applications with infrequent usage patterns.
  • Configure and validate your EWSAllowedAppIDs list before the rollout reaches your cloud.
  • Ensure EWSEnabled is set to True if continued EWS access is required.
  • Keep the EWSAllowedAppIDs list current as applications are added, removed, or migrated away from EWS.
  • Plan for up to a 24-hour propagation delay after changes are made to the EWSAllowedAppIDs list.

Microsoft's safeguard helps reduce the risk of service disruption but does not replace customer review and validation of EWSAllowedAppIDs.

We also recommend continuing plans to migrate applications from EWS to Microsoft Graph before EWS retirement is completed.

Together, these settings help deliver more predictable, on-brand PowerPoint presentations while reducing manual editing and review effort.

Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Page editors with a Copilot license can interact with generative AI directly within the SharePoint page editing experience using natural language chat prompts to plan, create, and modify content.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Access to the feature is governed by Microsoft Copilot license assignment. Only users assigned a Copilot license can access the AI authoring panel. There is no additional tenant-level toggle specific to this feature.
Does the change allow users to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. While the feature is available by default for Copilot-licensed users, users can choose when to use AI during page editing and can switch between AI-assisted editing and standard manual editing at any time.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) eSignature for Microsoft 365 - Recipient groups

We are introducing recipient groups for eSignature in Microsoft 365. Recipient groups allow a single recipient slot to be assigned to multiple people, where the first person to sign fulfills the signing requirement. This update helps make signature workflows more reliable by reducing delays when a specific signer is unavailable, without changing existing tenant policies.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 560822.

  • Microsoft 365 tenants that use eSignature for Microsoft 365

What will happen

  • Users can assign up to 10 people to a single recipient slot: 

  • The first person in the recipient group to sign fulfills the signing requirement for the group.
  • Signature workflows are less likely to stall due to individual signer availability.
  • The feature is enabled by default and respects existing tenant policies.

QuestionAnswer

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Viva Glint: Copilot features are no longer available for cross-tenant guest users
item.description:

Copilot in Viva Glint relies on Microsoft Copilot large language model (LLM) services. These underlying services do not currently support cross-tenant guest users. Previously, affected users might have experienced authentication errors or Copilot features that failed to load. To provide a more consistent experience, Viva Glint now hides the affected Copilot features for these users instead of displaying errors.

This change is not related to licensing or Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) policy settings.

  • Viva Glint administrators and support teams that support those users

  • Microsoft Entra ID

item.title: [planForChange] [Whiteboard] Legacy Whiteboard migration to OneDrive
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft Whiteboard is completing its transition from legacy Azure-backed storage to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards. Organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Whiteboards must migrate them to OneDrive-backed storage before migration tooling is retired - September 25, 2026. After September 25, 2026, remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated and can be only exported until October 16, 2026. After October 16, 2026, any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.

Key dates

  1. Before September 25, 2026: Users can still trigger migration, retry failed migrations, and export important content.
  2. September 25, 2026: Migration tooling is retired. Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  3. October 16, 2026: Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards are permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  4. November 30, 2026: Legacy Azure Whiteboard service shuts down.

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on late September 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

This change impacts organizations that still have legacy Azure-based Microsoft Whiteboards that have not yet been migrated to OneDrive-backed storage.

After September 25, 2026:

  • Users will no longer be able to migrate remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards.
  • Remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards become read-only and can no longer be migrated, but can still be viewed and exported until October 16, 2026.
  • Organizations that have not completed migration risk losing access to business content stored in legacy Whiteboards.

After October 16, 2026:

  • Any remaining legacy Azure-based Whiteboards will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered.
  • Enterprise users should access Microsoft Whiteboard through Teams and supported web experiences.

Organizations that have already completed migration to OneDrive-backed Whiteboards will not experience changes to existing OneDrive-backed content. New Whiteboards are already created in OneDrive-backed storage.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Admins should take the following actions immediately:

  • Inventory remaining legacy Whiteboards: Use the WhiteboardAdmin PowerShell module to identify Azure-based Whiteboards that still require migration.
  • Communicate with affected users:
  • Notify Whiteboard owners of the migration deadline (September 25, 2026) and deletion deadline (October 16, 2026).
  • Encourage users to migrate, export, or preserve any business-critical content before the deadlines.
  • Validate migration completion: Review migration status and confirm that important Whiteboards, permissions, and user access have been successfully migrated and remain accessible in OneDrive-backed storage.
  • Plan for large-scale migrations: For inactive users, orphaned Whiteboards, or large migration volumes, consider using the administrator-driven migration approach documented by Microsoft Whiteboard engineering.
  • Update internal guidance: Update user training materials, help documentation, and support procedures to direct users to Microsoft Whiteboard in Teams and supported web experiences rather than standalone applications.
  • Act before migration tooling is retired: After September 25, 2026, migration tooling will no longer be available, and no further migration path will exist for remaining legacy Whiteboards.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Lobby visibility will align with the "Who can admit from lobby" meeting option
item.description:
Updated September 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

We're updating the Microsoft Teams meeting lobby experience to improve privacy and align lobby visibility with existing meeting controls.

Today, the Who can admit from lobby option determines which meeting roles can admit people from the lobby, but it does not control who can see participants waiting in the lobby. As a result, some participants may be able to view the lobby even when they cannot admit attendees.

This change creates a more consistent and privacy-focused experience by aligning lobby visibility with lobby management permissions.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early September 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026 (previously mid-September)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams meeting organizers, co-organizers, presenters, and attendees
  • Organizations that use the Who can admit from lobby option

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams desktop apps
  • Microsoft Teams mobile apps

What will happen

  • Lobby visibility will align with the Who can admit from lobby meeting option. Only users who are permitted to admit participants from the lobby will be able to see participants waiting in the lobby.
  • For example, when Who can admit from lobby is set to Organizers and co-organizers only, presenters and attendees will no longer see participants waiting in the lobby. Only organizers and co-organizers will be able to view and manage lobby admissions.
  • This change is enabled automatically and does not require configuration.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend informing meeting organizers about this change if they currently rely on presenters to monitor the lobby during meetings. Organizations should review any meeting workflows that depend on presenters having visibility into lobby participants.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.
